title: JoiNMe: Association Construction
text: joinme supports following transformation families association features: Identity (type = "identity"): transformation. Functional (type = "functional"): user-defined mathematical expression. Monotone -spline (type = "ispline" "ispline_penalised"): smooth monotone mapping. Bounded-domain monotone -spline (type = "ispline_expit" "ispline_expit_penalised"): monotone spline machinery, applied plogis(x) rather directly x. Ordered piecewise linear (type = "pwlin"): posterior interpolation across fixed knots estimated monotone knot ordinates. Syntax: list(type = "identity") Default transform term omitted set NULL. parameters used. Syntax: list(type = "functional", expr = ~ log1p(x)) Required field: expr. defaults beyond supplied expression. Syntax: list(type = "ispline", knots = c(-1, 0, 1), coeff = c(0, 0.3, 0.8, 1.1, 1.3)) Required fields: knots, coeff. Default: degree = 3 omitted. Syntax: list(type = "ispline_penalised", x = seq(-2, 2, length.= 50), n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1) Defaults: n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1. knots omitted curve estimated, derived x quantiles. Syntax: list(type = "ispline_expit_penalised", x = seq(0.02, 0.98, length.= 50), n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1) Defaults: n_knots = 6, degree = 3, lambda = 1. raw association feature mapped plogis(x) runtime, spline basis built bounded domain. Supply training x explicit knots directly expit scale [0, 1] fitted spline domain matches runtime basis. Syntax: list(type = "pwlin", knots = c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), direction = "increasing"). Required field: knots (aliases: cutpoints earlier x). Default: direction = "increasing"; use "decreasing" falling transform. Note important perspective modelling. optional non-negative lambda penalises second differences ordered knot ordinates; defaults zero.

title: JoiNMe: Association Construction
text: functional evaluator supports common arithmetic functions log, exp, sqrt, sin, cos, tanh, plus aliases sigmoid/expit, softplus/log1p_exp, helpers like cbrt power.
code: transforms <- list(   cv_total = list(     type = "functional",     expr = ~ sinh(x) + tanh(x)   ),   cs_total = list(     type = "identity"   ),   corr = list(     type = "identity"   ) ) transforms <- list(   cv_total = list(type = "functional", expr = ~ inv_logit(x)),   cv_mean = list(type = "functional", expr = ~ exp(0.2 * x)),   cv_marker = list(type = "functional", expr = ~ power(x, 2)),   cs_total = list(type = "functional", expr = ~ sqrt(abs(x) + 1e-6)),   corr = list(type = "functional", expr = ~ cbrt(x)) )

title: JoiNMe: Association Construction
text: type = "ispline", specify transform shape following splines2::iSpline() convention: knots: knot locations (first last boundary knots), coeff: non-negative -spline basis coefficients, degree: spline degree (usually 3). Defaults: degree = 3 omitted. knots coeff must supplied explicitly. type = "ispline_expit", direct specification applies, except -spline basis evaluated plogis(x). runtime association feature still shown raw scale, transform’s knots must supplied expit scale spline domain. highly expremental meant stabilising boundary knots (usually unknown). may want standardise longitudinal outcome association squashed 0 1, plogis(x) flat outside range [-5, 5]. may also want put knots extreme values plogis(x) overcome flatness transform.
code: transforms <- list(   cv_total = list(     type = "ispline",     knots = c(-1, 0, 1),     coeff = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.2, 1.5, 1.6),     degree = 3   ),   cs_total = list(     type = "identity"   ),   corr = list(     type = "identity"   ) )

title: JoiNMe: Association Construction
text: type = "ispline_penalised", two supported modes: Simulation mode: provide x y define fixed monotone curve. Modelling mode: omit y, retain knots (n_knots) plus lambda, estimate monotone spline jointly rest model. Meaning arguments: x: raw association-feature values, used either training inputs help choose knots. y: optional target transformed values x points. present, telling package shape want approximate. lambda: smoothness penalty weight (higher = smoother, lower = flexible). Defaults: n_knots = 6 knots omitted. degree = 3 omitted. lambda = 1.0 omitted. helper-based plug-fitting, weights = NULL means equal weights diff_order = 2 default penalty order.
code: transforms <- list(   cv_total = list(     type = "identity"   ),   cs_total = list(     type = "identity"   ),   corr = list(     type = "ispline_penalised",     x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 40),     y = exp(seq(-2, 2, length.out = 40)),     n_knots = 6,     degree = 3,     lambda = 1.0   ) ) transforms <- list(   corr = list(     type = "ispline_penalised",     x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 40),     n_knots = 6,     degree = 3,     lambda = 1.0   ) )

title: JoiNMe: Association Construction
text: model fitting, raw association feature divided fixed knots, association values knots supplied outcome-like y vector. K knots, model estimates K-1 simplex \boldsymbol{\zeta}. relative transform ordinate knot j f_j = s \sum_{r=1}^{j-1} \zeta_r, \qquad s = \begin{cases}   1, & \text{increasing}, \\   -1, & \text{decreasing}. \end{cases} Thus f_1=0, f_K=s, every adjacent difference requested sign. Linear interpolation used knots boundary ordinates held constant outside knot range. survival contribution \alpha f(x): \alpha estimates total log-hazard span simplex estimates span distributed across intervals.
code: transforms <- list(   cv_total = list(     type = "identity"   ),   cs_total = list(     type = "identity"   ),   corr = list(     type = "pwlin",     knots = c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2),     direction = "increasing"   ) )

title: Independent standard-deviation and correlation regression
text: Marker--subject random effects describe departures specific one subject one longitudinal marker. covariance need constant across subjects. treatment may alter variability departures without altering dependence, whilst baseline physiological measurement may alter dependence without changing marginal variability. single covariance formula express hypotheses independently. joinme therefore separates covariance regression : standard-deviation regression, declared formulaVCov$sd; -diagonal unit-lower-triangular factor regression, declared formulaVCov$corr.

code: covariance_formula <- list(   sd = ~ treatment + age,   corr = ~ baseline_score ) formulaVCov = ~ treatment + age  # exactly equivalent to formulaVCov = list(   sd = ~ treatment + age,   corr = ~ treatment + age )

text: Let Q dimension marker--subject random-effect basis. subject , joinme reconstructs L_i=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\sigma_i)K_i, \boldsymbol{\sigma}_i=(\sigma_{i1},\ldots,\sigma_{iQ})^\top contains marginal standard deviations K_i Cholesky correlation factor. marker--subject effect marker d \boldsymbol w_{id}=L_i\boldsymbol z_{w,id}, \qquad \boldsymbol z_{w,id}\sim N_Q(\boldsymbol0,I_Q). Let \boldsymbol x_{sd,} design row produced formulaVCov$sd. coordinate r=1,\ldots,Q, \eta^{sd}_{ir} = \alpha^{sd}_r +\boldsymbol x_{sd,}^{\top}\boldsymbol\beta^{sd}_r +\lambda_{m(r)}z_{L,,m(r)}. marginal standard deviation \sigma_{ir}=g_{sd}(\eta^{sd}_{ir}), g_{sd} softplus default may changed exponential link control = list(vcov_diag_link = "exp"). Let \boldsymbol x_{corr,} independent design row produced formulaVCov$corr. row-major -diagonal coordinate h=(r,c), c<r, \eta^{K}_{ih} = \alpha^{K}_h +\boldsymbol x_{corr,}^{\top}\boldsymbol\beta^{K}_h +\lambda_{m(h)}z_{L,,m(h)}, \qquad p_{,rc}=\tanh(\eta^{K}_{ih}),\ c<r. partial correlations form one row Cholesky correlation factor K_{,rc}=p_{,rc}\prod_{h<c}\sqrt{1-p_{,rh}^2},\quad c<r, \qquad K_{,rr}=\prod_{h<r}\sqrt{1-p_{,rh}^2}. upper triangle zero every row norm one. covariance matrix \Sigma_i=L_iL_i^{\top} =\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\sigma_i)K_iK_i^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\sigma_i). independent regression design: SD model sets \boldsymbol\sigma_i, dependence model sets row-wise partial correlations. -diagonal regression absent nested marker--subject term uses ||, signalling iid random effect structure. one non-negative scalar \lambda_m covariance coordinate. Collectively, \boldsymbol\lambda_L vector, dense matrix. action \operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol\lambda_L)\boldsymbol z_{L,}, latent coordinate m affects predictor coordinate m. ordinary model, \lambda_m^2 conditional residual variance untransformed predictor. final standard deviation, correlation, covariance.

code: sim_comp <- simulate_joinme(   n_id = 40,   families = rep("student_t", 3),   times_obs = seq(0, 8, length.out = 12),   seed = 444,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   truth = jm_truth(assoc_coef = list(slope = c(cv_total = 0.6))) )  # Simulate cause-specific event times and derive event_type from the minimum time. set.seed(444) cause_levels <- c("cause1", "cause2") time_cens <- 8.0  h0_list <- list(   cause1 = weibull_h0(shape = 1.2, scale = 5.0),   cause2 = weibull_h0(shape = 2.0, scale = 7.0) )  gamma_w_mat <- rbind(   cause1 = c("(Intercept)" = -0.2, "x1" = 0.4, "x2" = -0.3),   cause2 = c("(Intercept)" = 0.1, "x1" = -0.2, "x2" = 0.5) )  find_bracket <- function(f, lower = 0, upper = 1, upper_max = 50, expand = 1.7, max_expand = 60L) {   f_lower <- f(lower)   if (!is.finite(f_lower) || f_lower > 0) return(NULL)   f_upper <- f(upper)   if (!is.finite(f_upper)) return(NULL)   it <- 0L   while (f_upper < 0 && upper < upper_max && it < max_expand) {     upper <- min(upper_max, upper * expand)     f_upper <- f(upper)     if (!is.finite(f_upper)) return(NULL)     it <- it + 1L   }   if (f_upper >= 0) list(lower = lower, upper = upper) else NULL }  draw_cause_time <- function(i, k) {   haz_row <- c("(Intercept)" = 1, "x1" = sim_comp$dataEvent$x1[i], "x2" = sim_comp$dataEvent$x2[i])   eta_w <- sum(haz_row * gamma_w_mat[k, ])   alpha_cv <- sim_comp$truth$alpha_cv_total   h0 <- h0_list[[k]]    hazard_i <- function(t) h0(t) * exp(eta_w + alpha_cv * sim_comp$helpers$cv_total(i, t))   cumhaz_i <- function(t) {     if (t <= 0) return(0)     out <- integrate(hazard_i, lower = 0, upper = t, rel.tol = 1e-6, subdivisions = 2000L)     as.numeric(out$value)   }    U <- runif(1)   target <- -log(U)   f_root <- function(t) cumhaz_i(t) - target   br <- find_bracket(f_root, lower = 0, upper = 1, upper_max = 50)   if (is.null(br)) return(list(time = time_cens, event = 0L))   T <- uniroot(f_root, lower = br$lower, upper = br$upper)$root   if (T > time_cens) list(time = time_cens, event = 0L) else list(time = T, event = 1L) }  event_time <- numeric(nrow(sim_comp$dataEvent)) event_type <- character(nrow(sim_comp$dataEvent)) event_flag <- integer(nrow(sim_comp$dataEvent))  for (i in seq_len(nrow(sim_comp$dataEvent))) {   times_k <- vapply(cause_levels, function(k) draw_cause_time(i, k)$time, numeric(1))   min_idx <- which.min(times_k)   event_time[i] <- times_k[min_idx]   event_flag[i] <- as.integer(event_time[i] < time_cens)   event_type[i] <- cause_levels[min_idx]   if (event_flag[i] == 0L) {     event_type[i] <- cause_levels[1]   } }  sim_comp$dataEvent$time <- event_time sim_comp$dataEvent$event <- event_flag sim_comp$dataEvent$event_type <- factor(event_type, levels = cause_levels)  sim_comp$dataLong <- sim_comp$dataLong |>   dplyr::inner_join(sim_comp$dataEvent[, c("id", "time")], by = "id", suffix = c("", "_event")) |>   dplyr::filter(time <= time_event) |>   dplyr::select(-time_event) formulaLong_comp <- y ~ 1 + time + x1 +   (1 + time || id) +   (0 + x1 + (1 + time || id) || marker)  formulaEvent_comp <- survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1 + x1 + x2  fit_comp <- joinme(   formulaLong = formulaLong_comp,   dataLong = sim_comp$dataLong,   formulaEvent = formulaEvent_comp,   dataEvent = sim_comp$dataEvent,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   families = rep("student_t", 3),   transforms = joinme_tf(cv_total = "identity"),   event_type_var = "event_type",   control = list(     engine = "cmdstanr",     chains = 1,     parallel_chains = 1,     iter_warmup = 150,     iter_sampling = 150,     seed = 444,     refresh = 0,     adapt_delta = 0.85,     max_treedepth = 10   ) ) id_comp <- 1 ndL_comp <- sim_comp$dataLong[sim_comp$dataLong$id == id_comp, ] ndE_comp <- sim_comp$dataEvent[sim_comp$dataEvent$id == id_comp, ]  time_start_comp <- max(ndL_comp$time) times_comp <- seq(time_start_comp, time_start_comp + 2, length.out = 40)  pred_comp <- predict(   fit_comp,   newdataLong = ndL_comp,   newdataEvent = ndE_comp,   process = "event",   time_start = time_start_comp,   times = times_comp,   control = list(     n_samples = 100,     engine = "cmdstanr",     chains = 1,     iter_warmup = 0,     iter_sampling = 1,     fixed_param = TRUE,     refresh = 0   ) )  plot(pred_comp, type = "survival")

title: The JoiNMe Framework: Methodology and Statistical Theory
text: Joint modelling longitudinal survival data standard approach analysing time-dependent covariates measured error [1]. many clinical observational settings, subject status monitored via multiple biomarkers (example, blood pressure, bilirubin, cognitive scores) alongside terminal event (example, death, dropout). Standard approaches often face two limitations: Computational Scalability: number markers D increases, dimension random effects vector grows linearly quadratically, creating identifiablity issue numerical integration MCMC sampling. Rigidity: Models often assume Gaussian error terms linear associations, limiting applicability skewed data non-linear biological mechanisms. JoiNMe addresses challenges structural decomposition linear predictor flexible distributional regression framework. vignette outlines statistical theory governing package.

title: The JoiNMe Framework: Methodology and Statistical Theory
text: Let \mathcal{D}_i = \{y_{id}(t_{ij}) : j = 1, \dots, n_{id}, d = 1, \dots, D\} denote observed longitudinal data subject , y_{id}(t) response marker d time t. assume generalised linear mixed models (GLMMs) marker, linked via shared latent structure. linear predictor \eta_{id}(t) subject marker d time t decomposed fixed effects, shared random effects, marker-specific deviations: \eta_{id}(t) = \mathbf{x}_{id}(t)^\top \boldsymbol{\beta} + \mathbf{z}^{(id)}_{}(t)^\top \mathbf{u}_i + \mathbf{z}^{(mk)}_{d}(t)^\top \mathbf{v}_d + \mathbf{z}^{(idm)}_{id}(t)^\top \mathbf{w}_{id} : Fixed Effects (\boldsymbol{\beta}): Capture population-level trends across covariates \mathbf{x}. Shared Subject Effects (\mathbf{u}_i \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \Sigma_u)): Represents underlying “frailty” shared process common markers subject (e.g., general health status). Marker-Specific Random Effects (\mathbf{v}_d \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \Sigma_v)): Captures heterogeneity marker trajectories common across subjects (e.g., marker-specific baseline levels rates change). Marker--Subject Interactions (\mathbf{w}_{id} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \Sigma_{w,})): Captures specific deviation marker d subject shared trends. hierarchical structure allows information sharing across markers (shrinking estimates towards shared process \mathbf{u}_i) maintaining flexibility individual marker dynamics. observed response y_{id}(t) generated distribution \mathcal{F} location parameter linked \eta_{id}(t) potentially ancillary parameters \boldsymbol{\psi}_{d}: y_{id}(t) \sim \mathcal{F}_d(\cdot | \eta_{id}(t), \boldsymbol{\psi}_{d}) JoiNMe supports wide range families \mathcal{F}_d, including: Gaussian / Student’s t: continuous, potentially heavy-tailed data. Beta: bounded (0,1) proportions. Bernoulli / Binomial: binary count--success data. Poisson / Negative Binomial: count data. Double Exponential / Skew Double Exponential: continuous outcomes Laplace tails , required, asymmetric conditional quantiles. Cumulative Logit: ordinal outcomes. Furthermore, distributional parameters (example, residual scale \sigma) can modelled functions covariates (distributional regression):  \log(\sigma_{id}(t)) = \mathbf{x}_{\sigma, id}(t)^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}_\sigma joinem also supports family-scoped distributional regressions using bracket syntax left-hand side, e.g. sigma[family=student_t] ~ 1 + time sigma[family=gaussian] ~ 1 + x1 scopes estimated separate coefficient blocks contribute rows scoped family. Without brackets (example, sigma ~ ...), formula applies rows parameter exists. skew double exponential distribution, JoiNMe uses quantile parameterisation. Given location \mu, scale \sigma>0, 0<\tau<1, density f(y\mid\mu,\sigma,\tau) = \frac{2\tau(1-\tau)}{\sigma} \begin{cases} \exp\{-2(1-\tau)|y-\mu|/\sigma\}, & y<\mu,\\ \exp\{-2\tau|y-\mu|/\sigma\}, & y\geq\mu. \end{cases} Thus \mu conditional \tau-quantile, \tau=0.5 recovers vthe symmetric Laplace distribution. marker-specific fixed value declared jm_family("skew_laplace", tau = 0.8). omitted, tau estimated tau ~ ... distributional regression present, family-level constant otherwise. title: joinme
text: JoiNMe (package name styled joinme deliberate ambiguity) fits Bayesian nested mixed-effects models multivariate longitudinal markers, either alone jointly time--event outcomes. supports multiple outcome families (Gaussian, Student-t, binary, count, beta, ordinal, skewed families) irregular measurement schedules. Current implementation experiments flexible association structures, covariance regression, transform-based modelling nonlinear effects, dynamic prediction. joinme works CmdStanR RStan. package designed recipes : simulate assemble longitudinal event data simulate_joinme(), fit joint model joinme(), inspect posterior draws diagnostics, summarise plot fitted effects, generate dynamic predictions plot future trajectories survival.

text: can scope distributional regressions family using square brackets LHS: sigma ~ 1 + time sigma[family=student_t] ~ 1 + time sigma[family=gaussian] ~ 1 + x1 Allowed distributional parameters: sigma nu phi alpha (aliases: alpha_skew, skew) kappa: positive Beta sample size, giving shape parameters mu * kappa (1 - mu) * kappa tau: skew-double-exponential quantile/asymmetry parameter (0, 1). may modelled formulaDist, fixed one marker jm_family("skew_laplace", tau = 0.8). Example: fixed skew-Laplace quantile, place constant corresponding marker family rather control: families declaration can passed simulate_joinme(). simulator uses marker-specific constant generate outcomes records returned distributional truth. tau = 0.5 gives symmetric Laplace distribution. endpoints excluded: tau = 0 tau = 1 degenerate limits rather valid skew-Laplace distributions.

text: Trinh Dong, 2026
code: library(joinme)  set.seed(1)  # Simulate a small dataset sim <- simulate_joinme(   n_id = 10,   families = list(     jm_family("student_t"),     jm_family("student_t", inv_link = ~ inv_logit(x / 2))   ),   times_obs = seq(0, 5, length.out = 8),   quadrature_nodes = 31,   seed = 2026,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   truth = jm_truth(assoc_coef = list(slope = c(cv_total = 0.6))) )  # Note: when estimating marker weights, compare to sim$truth$marker_weights # because effective marker intensities are used directly from w_raw inside Stan.  formulaLong <- y ~ 1 + time + x1 +   (1 + time | id) +   (0 + x1 + (1 + time | id) | marker)  formulaEvent <- survival::Surv(time, event) ~ 1 + x1 + x2  fit <- joinme(   formulaLong = formulaLong,   dataLong = sim$dataLong,   formulaEvent = formulaEvent,   dataEvent = sim$dataEvent,   assoc = c("cv_total"),   families = list(     jm_family("student_t"),     jm_family("student_t", inv_link = ~ inv_logit(x / 2))   ),   transforms = list(cv_total = list(type = "identity")),   control = list(     parallel_chains = 1,     iter_warmup = 100,     iter_sampling = 100,     seed = 2026,     refresh = 0,     adapt_delta = 0.9   ) )  inherits(fit, "JoiNMeFit")  # Summaries summary(fit) diagnosis(fit) fixef(fit) coef(fit)  # Renamed posterior draws posterior_draws(fit, variables = c("time", "alpha_cv_total"), format = "draws_df")  # Bayesplot-backed posterior display with renamed variables mcmc_plot(fit, variable = c("time", "alpha_cv_total"), type = "trace")  # Conditional effects for either joint-model process profiles <- make_conditions(sim$dataEvent, vars = "x1") ce <- conditional_effects(   fit,   effects = list(longitudinal = "time", event = "x1"),   conditions = profiles,   process = c("longitudinal", "event"),   plot = FALSE ) plot(ce, ask = FALSE)  # Average marker-specific expected responses after applying each inverse link ce_average_marker <- conditional_effects(   fit,   effects = "time",   process = "longitudinal",   longitudinal_estimand = "marginal_marker",   plot = FALSE )  # Paired posterior contrast between two covariate profiles contrast_profiles <- data.frame(   time = seq(0, 5, length.out = 40),   x2 = 0,   cond__ = paste0("time=", round(seq(0, 5, length.out = 40), 2)) ) cc <- conditional_contrast(   fit,   groupA = c(x1 = 1),   groupB = c(x1 = -1),   conditions = contrast_profiles,   process = c("longitudinal", "event"),   longitudinal_estimand = "marginal_marker",   plot = FALSE ) plot(cc, condition_variable = "time", ask = FALSE)  # Random effects / covariance / combined coefficients (nested by formula block) re_fit <- ranef(fit) cf_fit <- coef(fit) vc_fit <- vcov(fit) # Example accessors: # re_fit$formulaLong$id # cf_fit$formulaLong$id # re_fit$formulaDist$sigma$allFamilies # vc_fit$formulaDist$nu$allFamilies  # Dynamic prediction for one subject ndL <- sim$dataLong[sim$dataLong$id == 1, ] ndE <- sim$dataEvent[sim$dataEvent$id == 1, ] time_start <- max(ndL$time)  pred <- posterior_epred(   fit,   newdataLong = ndL,   newdataEvent = ndE,   time_start = time_start,   times = seq(time_start, time_start + 1, length.out = 20),   control = list(n_samples = 50),   seed = 69 )  # Prediction diagnostics + conditional random-effect summaries summary(pred) diagnosis(pred)  # Available only when marker covariance depends on id if (isTRUE(pred$metadata$marker_corr_depends_on_id)) {   re_pred <- ranef(pred)   vc_pred <- vcov(pred) }  # Plot longitudinal and survival predictions plot(pred, type = c("longitudinal", "survival"), combined = TRUE) longitudinal_plot(pred) survival_plot(pred)  # Alternative longitudinal display: posterior mean change heatmap plot(   fit,   type = "longitudinal",   longitudinal_style = "heatmap",   scale = "epred",   threshold = 0.05 )  # title: Example: Build Transform Specification from Formula String — example_transform_spec
code: # Example 1: Functional transformation (bytecode-backed) spec_cv <- list(   type = "functional",   expr = ~ (log(sqrt(x + 1/inv_logit(3*x - 3))))^2 )  # Example 2: Piecewise-linear spec_cs <- list(   type = "pwlin",   knots = c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2),   direction = "increasing" )  # Example 3: I-spline (monotonic) # - knots define basis locations (first/last are boundary knots) # - coeff defines the monotone shape directly spec_corr <- list(   type = "ispline",   knots = c(-1, 0, 1),   coeff = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.2, 1.5),   degree = 3 )  # Example 4: Penalised monotone I-spline (fit in R) # - x is the input scale of the raw association feature # - y is the desired transformed output at each x # - lambda controls smoothness (higher = smoother) spec_corr_pen <- list(   type = "ispline_penalised",   x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 50),   y = exp(seq(-2, 2, length.out = 50)),   n_knots = 6,   degree = 3,   lambda = 1.0,   direction = "increasing" )  # Example 5: Penalised monotone I-spline (Stan-estimated coefficients) # - omit y so Stan learns the monotone shape directly # - if knots are omitted, n_knots = 6 and x quantiles define them spec_corr_pen_stan <- list(   type = "ispline_penalised",   x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 50),   n_knots = 6,   degree = 3,   lambda = 1.0 )  # Example 6: Penalised monotone I-spline on expit(x) spec_corr_expit <- list(   type = "ispline_expit_penalised",   x = seq(0.02, 0.98, length.out = 50),   y = seq(0.02, 0.98, length.out = 50)^0.75,   n_knots = 6,   degree = 3,   lambda = 1.0,   direction = "increasing" )  # Combine and build standata transforms <- joinme_tf(   cv_total = spec_cv,   cs_total = spec_cs,   corr = spec_corr ) standata_tf <- build_standata_transforms(transforms)

JoiNMe uses function link supplied formula joinme_family(). Inversion proceeds outermost operation towards x.  Composed transformations consequently reversed correct order.  example, ~ log(2 * x + 1) becomes ~ (exp(x) - 1) / 2. supported one--one elementary pairs log/exp, logit/inv_logit, Phi/inv_Phi (pnorm/qnorm probit aliases), sinh/asinh, tanh/atanh, reciprocal, sqrt/square, cbrt/cube.  Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, powers finite non-zero constant also supported.  Arithmetic branches contain x must reduce numeric constants.  Even integer powers rejected one--one real line; deliberately restricted-domain inverse can instead declared explicitly inv_link. Expressions containing x , globally non-injective operations abs, sin, cos, cosh, rejected.  deliberate: silently selecting one branch define valid inverse-link full response domain.

text: jm_truth() describes population quantities used generate complete data set. coefficient hierarchy follows jm_priors(): global intercept slope declarations provide fallbacks, whilst named model components may replace either role. finite numeric vector fixes corresponding population coefficient. prior_*() declaration draws one coefficient vector beginning simulation. realised vector held constant every subject, marker observation recorded returned simulation's truth. Thus, distribution supplied describes variation simulated data sets, variation observations within one data set. declaration also contains baseline hazard covariance parameters ordinary random-effect blocks. random-effect standard deviation omitted, one value per coefficient drawn Exponential(1). correlation matrix omitted, one matrix drawn LKJ distribution selected lkj. population distributions used Stan fitting model.

title: Functional Transform Builder for Joint Models — parse_transform_expr
text: Functional bytecode vector operation codes (0-27) paired vector constant values. Constants embedded using PUSH_CONST operations. Phi denotes standard normal cumulative distribution function, whereas inv_Phi probit denote quantile function. deliberately assigned different instructions domains ranges differ.

title: Functional Transform Builder for Joint Models — parse_transform_expr
text: 0 PUSH_X: Push input x onto stack 1 PUSH_CONST: Push next constant value 2 ADD: Pop b,; push +b 3 SUB: Pop b,; push -b 4 MUL: Pop b,; push *b 5 DIV: Pop b,; push /b 6 LOG: Pop ; push log() 7 EXP: Pop ; push exp() 8 SQRT: Pop ; push sqrt() 9 INV_LOGIT: Pop ; push inv_logit() 10 LOGIT: Pop ; push logit() 11 RECIPROCAL: Pop ; push 1/12 POW: Pop b,; push ^b 13 SIN: Pop ; push sin() 14 COS: Pop ; push cos() 15 TAN: Pop ; push tan() 16 ABS: Pop ; push abs() 17 SQUARE: Pop ; push ^2 18 SINH: Pop ; push sinh() 19 COSH: Pop ; push cosh() 20 TANH: Pop ; push tanh() 21 ASINH: Pop ; push asinh() 22 ACOSH: Pop ; push acosh() 23 ATANH: Pop ; push atanh() 24 SOFTPLUS: Pop ; push log1p_exp() 25 CBRT: Pop ; push cbrt() 26 PHI: Pop ; push standard normal CDF \(\Phi()\) 27 INV_PHI: Pop ; push standard normal quantile \(\Phi^{-1}()\)

title: Functional Transform Builder for Joint Models — parse_transform_expr
code: # Simple: f(x) = x + 2 bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ x + 2)  # Use a plain formula (recommended) bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ log(x + 1)) # Returns: bytecode = c(0, 1, 2), const_data = c(2)  # Complex: f(x) = (log(sqrt(x + 1/inv_logit(3*x - 3))))^2 bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ (log(sqrt(x + 1/inv_logit(3*x - 3))))^2)  # The normal CDF and its quantile use separate instructions phi_bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ Phi(x)) probit_bc <- parse_transform_expr(~ inv_Phi(x))
